issues.legal_issue: An agreement between litigants that one will not defend a suit constitutes collusion only when it is an improper act or omission intended to achieve a dishonest purpose.
material_facts: The lessee agreed not to contest the landlord’s possession suit, and the suit proceeded to an ex parte decree.
The challenge to the decree relied on the agreement not to defend and the circumstances surrounding the suit, but no dishonest purpose was established.
issues.conclusion: The agreement not to defend, without proof that it was made to achieve a dishonest purpose, did not establish collusion; the decree was not proved to have been procured collusively.
issues.legal_principle: Collusion is an improper act, or improper refraining from an act, for a dishonest purpose, or a secret arrangement to obtain a judicial decision for a sinister purpose. The Court relied on Scott v. Scott and Nagubai Ammal v. B. Shamma Rao. An agreement that a defendant will not defend a suit does not, by itself, satisfy that test.

rule.if: collusion_challenge_proceeding and agreement_not_to_defend and not dishonest_purpose_proven

predicates.collusion_challenge_proceeding: A party brings a proceeding to challenge a decree on the ground that the litigants procured it collusively.
predicates.agreement_not_to_defend: One litigant agrees with the other not to defend the suit.
predicates.dishonest_purpose_proven: The evidence establishes that the agreement or another act or omission was intended to achieve a dishonest purpose.
predicates.decree_not_proven_collusive: The decree is not established to have been procured collusively.

issues.definition: When a decree is challenged as collusive, an agreement not to defend does not establish collusion if no dishonest purpose is proven.

issues.legal_issue: A landlord’s omission to implead a sub-lessee in a possession suit against the lessee is not, by itself, an improper act where the law permits the suit to proceed without the sub-lessee and the decree binds the sub-lessee.
material_facts: The landlord sued its lessee for possession without joining the sub-lessee.
The applicable law permitted the landlord to sue the lessee without joining the sub-lessee, and a decree in such a suit would bind the sub-lessee.
issues.conclusion: The landlord’s omission to join the sub-lessee was not improper and did not establish collusion.
issues.legal_principle: The law permits a landlord to seek possession from a lessee without impleading the sub-lessee; the resulting decree may bind the sub-lessee. Although that consequence may operate harshly, the omission to join the sub-lessee is not improper where the law allows it.

rule.if: landlord_possession_proceeding and sublessee_omitted and joinder_not_required_by_law and decree_binds_sublessee

predicates.landlord_possession_proceeding: A landlord brings a possession suit against its lessee.
predicates.sublessee_omitted: The landlord does not join the lessee’s sub-lessee in the suit.
predicates.joinder_not_required_by_law: The applicable law does not require the sub-lessee to be joined in that suit.
predicates.decree_binds_sublessee: A decree in the suit binds the sub-lessee.
predicates.omission_to_join_sublessee_not_improper: The landlord’s omission to join the sub-lessee is not an improper act.

issues.definition: In a landlord’s possession suit against a lessee, omitting the sub-lessee is not improper when joinder is not required and the decree binds the sub-lessee.

issues.legal_issue: A defendant’s decision not to defend a possession suit is not, without more, an improper act establishing collusion.
material_facts: The lessee did not contest the landlord’s suit for possession.
No plausible defence that the lessee could have raised against the landlord’s claim was suggested or established.
issues.conclusion: The lessee’s failure to defend the suit was not shown to be improper and did not establish collusion.
issues.legal_principle: A defendant is not bound to raise a defence merely because one might be available. In the circumstances considered, no plausible defence to the possession claim was identified; the failure to defend therefore did not establish an improper omission or dishonest purpose.

predicates.possession_suit_between_landlord_and_les: A landlord sues its lessee for possession.
predicates.lessee_does_not_defend: The lessee does not contest the possession suit.
predicates.no_plausible_defence_established: No plausible defence available to the lessee against the possession claim is established.
predicates.failure_to_defend_not_improper: The lessee’s failure to defend is not, by itself, an improper act.

issues.definition: A lessee’s failure to defend a landlord’s possession suit is not improper when no plausible defence to the claim is established.

issues.legal_issue: Common directors do not, by themselves, make two companies the same legal entity or establish that a suit between them was collusive.
material_facts: The landlord and the lessee were distinct companies with the same directors and some common shareholder interests.
It was not alleged that the companies were in reality one person using two names, and the landlord genuinely sought possession.
issues.conclusion: The common directors and shareholder interests did not establish a dishonest or sinister purpose or collusion between the companies.
issues.legal_principle: Companies with common directors or shareholders remain distinct legal entities absent a basis to treat them as the same person. Their common management or interests alone do not show that a suit between them was brought for a dishonest or sinister purpose.

rule.if: collusion_challenge_proceeding and companies_have_common_directors and companies_are_distinct_entities and not evidence_companies_are_same_person

predicates.collusion_challenge_proceeding: A party challenges a decree on the ground that the litigants procured it collusively.
predicates.companies_have_common_directors: The companies involved in the suit have some or all of the same directors.
predicates.companies_are_distinct_entities: The companies have separate legal identities and conduct their affairs as distinct entities.
predicates.evidence_companies_are_same_person: Evidence establishes that the companies are in reality one person using different names.
predicates.common_directors_alone_do_not_establish_: Common directors alone do not establish that the suit was collusive.

issues.definition: In a challenge alleging collusion, common directors do not establish collusion when the companies remain distinct entities and there is no evidence that they are one person.

issues.legal_issue: Statutory protection for a sub-tenant against eviction by the sub-tenant’s own landlord does not protect the sub-tenant against eviction resulting from a possession suit brought by an upstream landlord against its lessee.
material_facts: The sub-lessee relied on the possibility that it was a protected tenant under the applicable tenancy legislation.
The possession suit was brought by the upstream landlord against the lessee, not by the lessee against the sub-lessee.
The interpretation that the legislation protected a tenant only against eviction by that tenant’s landlord was not challenged.
issues.conclusion: Even if the sub-lessee qualified for the statutory protection, it would not protect the sub-lessee against eviction resulting from the upstream landlord’s suit.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the interpretation of the Calcutta Thika Tenancy Act, 1949, in Shamsuddin Ahmad v. Dinanath Mullick: the Act protected a tenant against eviction by that tenant’s landlord, not against eviction from another source. The Court did not decide whether the sub-lessee qualified as a protected tenant.

predicates.eviction_protection_proceeding: A tenant relies on statutory protection in a proceeding concerning eviction.
predicates.tenant_claims_statutory_protection: The tenant claims protection against eviction by the tenant’s own landlord.
predicates.eviction_sought_by_upstream_landlord: A landlord higher in the chain of leases seeks possession from the tenant’s immediate landlord.
predicates.statutory_protection_does_not_bar_upstre: The claimed protection does not prevent eviction resulting from the upstream landlord’s suit.

issues.definition: Statutory protection against eviction by a tenant’s own landlord does not prevent eviction resulting from an upstream landlord’s possession suit.
